## Mermaid Diagram

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/docs/mermaid.html

Render Mermaid diagrams — flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts, and more — from text syntax directly on your Confluence page.

### How to Use

1. Type `/Mermaid` in the Confluence editor

2. A fullscreen editor opens with a code panel (left) and live preview (right)

3. Write your Mermaid syntax (e.g., `graph TD; A-->B; B-->C;`)

4. See the diagram update in real-time as you type

5. Click **Save** — the diagram renders on the published page

 Sample Script

[  Download .mmd ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openAPI-Studio/macro-toolkit-docs/main/assets/raw/mermaid-sample.mmd)

```
flowchart TD
    A[Start] --> B{Login Successful?}
    B -->|No| C[Show Error Message]
    C --> A
    B -->|Yes| D[Load Dashboard]
    D --> E{Choose Action}
    E -->|View Reports| F[Reports Module]
    E -->|Manage Tasks| G[Tasks Module]
    E -->|Settings| H[Settings Module]
    F --> I[Generate Report]
    G --> J[Create Task]
    H --> K[Update Preferences]
    I --> L[Save/Export]
    J --> L
    K --> L
    L --> M[Logout]
    M --> A
```

Editor — live preview as you type

![Mermaid Diagram editor with code and live preview](https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/assets/mermaid/mermaid_editscreen.png)

Published page

![Mermaid Diagram rendered on Confluence page](https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/assets/mermaid/mermaid_publish.png)

### Supported Diagram Types

- Flowcharts

- Sequence Diagrams

- Gantt Charts

- Class Diagrams

- State Diagrams

- Pie Charts

- ER Diagrams

- Git Graphs

### Pro Features PRO

The following features are available exclusively in the **Pro version**:

#### Export as SVG / PNG

Download your diagrams as high-resolution SVG or 2× PNG files. Available both in the editor toolbar and on the published page (hover to reveal export buttons).

#### Zoom Controls

Interactive zoom on the published diagram — use the +/− buttons or `Ctrl/⌘ + Scroll` to zoom in/out. Set a default zoom level (50%–200%) in the editor that persists on the page.

#### Code Split View & Copy

On the published page, click the `</> Code` button to open a split panel showing the raw Mermaid source with a one-click copy button.

#### Diagram Templates

8 built-in templates (Flowchart, Sequence, Class, State, Gantt, Pie, ER, Git Graph) — insert with one click from the editor toolbar.

#### Configurable Container Height

Set the minimum container height (Auto, 100px–600px) to control how the diagram fits on the page. Default is **Auto** (fits content exactly).

#### Dark Mode Support

Diagrams automatically adapt to Confluence's light/dark theme — text, lines, and backgrounds adjust for readability in both modes.

 Using via MCP (Model Context Protocol)

[  Download .md ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openAPI-Studio/macro-toolkit-docs/main/assets/raw/mermaid-mcp-guide.md)

Programmatically insert or update Mermaid diagrams via MCP using the Confluence storage format.

##### Macro Config Schema

| Field | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code | string | The Mermaid syntax source code | '' |
| minHeight | string | 'auto' or pixel value like '300' | 'auto' |
| defaultZoom | string | Zoom percentage: '50' to '200' | '100' |

##### Storage Format (XHTML)

```
<ac:structured-macro ac:name="mermaid-diagram" ac:schema-version="1" ac:macro-id="unique-id">
  <ac:parameter ac:name="code">graph TD
  A[Start] --&gt; B{Decision}
  B --&gt;|Yes| C[Done]
  B --&gt;|No| D[Retry]</ac:parameter>
  <ac:parameter ac:name="minHeight">auto</ac:parameter>
  <ac:parameter ac:name="defaultZoom">100</ac:parameter>
</ac:structured-macro>
```

**Important:** HTML-encode special characters (`>` → `&gt;`, `<` → `&lt;`, `&` → `&amp;`).

##### MCP Tool Definition

```
{
  "name": "insert_mermaid_diagram",
  "description": "Insert a Mermaid diagram into a Confluence page",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "pageId": { "type": "string", "description": "The Confluence page ID" },
      "code": { "type": "string", "description": "Mermaid diagram syntax" },
      "minHeight": { "type": "string", "default": "auto" },
      "defaultZoom": { "type": "string", "default": "100" }
    },
    "required": ["pageId", "code"]
  }
}
```

##### Implementation Pattern

```
async function insertMermaidDiagram({ pageId, code, minHeight = 'auto', defaultZoom = '100' }) {
  const page = await confluenceApi.get(`/wiki/api/v2/pages/${pageId}?body-format=storage`);

  const encodedCode = code
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;');

  const macroMarkup = `
<ac:structured-macro ac:name="mermaid-diagram" ac:schema-version="1">
  <ac:parameter ac:name="code">${encodedCode}</ac:parameter>
  <ac:parameter ac:name="minHeight">${minHeight}</ac:parameter>
  <ac:parameter ac:name="defaultZoom">${defaultZoom}</ac:parameter>
</ac:structured-macro>`;

  const newBody = page.body.storage.value + macroMarkup;
  await confluenceApi.put(`/wiki/api/v2/pages/${pageId}`, {
    version: { number: page.version.number + 1 },
    body: { storage: { value: newBody, representation: 'storage' } }
  });
}
```

##### Supported Diagram Types

- `graph TD/LR` Flowcharts

- `sequenceDiagram` Sequence

- `classDiagram` Class

- `stateDiagram-v2` State

- `erDiagram` ER

- `gantt` Gantt

- `pie` Pie

- `gitGraph` Git

- `mindmap` Mind maps

- `timeline` Timelines

##### Tips

1. **Validate** — Call `mermaid.parse(code)` before saving

2. **Escape** — Encode `< > & "` in the code field

3. **Newlines** — Use actual newlines, not `\n` literals

4. **Update** — Find `ac:name="mermaid-diagram"` block and replace code param

5. **Prerequisite** — Forge app must be installed on the site

### Technical Details

| Storage | Macro config (inline with page) |
| --- | --- |
| External Service | None — renders client-side |
| Editor | Fullscreen split-pane with line numbers, Tab support, debounced preview |
| Export | SVG & PNG (2× resolution) PRO |
| Zoom | Interactive (+/−/Fit, Ctrl+Scroll) with configurable default PRO |
| Code View | Split panel with copy button on published page PRO |
| Templates | 8 built-in (Flowchart, Sequence, Class, State, Gantt, Pie, ER, Git) PRO |
| Theme | Auto light/dark mode adaptation PRO |
| Availability | Basic editor in Lite; full features in Pro |

## 3D Viewer

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/docs/3d-viewer.html

Display interactive 3D models directly on your Confluence page. Supports STL, OBJ, GLB, and 3MF formats with full orbit controls, zoom, and pan.

PRO ONLY

Screenshot placeholder

### How to Use

1. Type `/3D Viewer` in the editor

2. Upload a 3D model file (STL, OBJ, GLB, or 3MF)

3. Configure display options (background color, lighting, rotation)

4. Click **Save** — the interactive 3D model renders on the page

5. Viewers can orbit, zoom, and pan the model interactively

### Supported Formats

##### .STL

Standard tessellation — 3D printing, CAD exports

##### .OBJ

Wavefront — widely supported, with materials

##### .GLB

Binary glTF — compact, web-optimized, with textures

##### .3MF

3D Manufacturing Format — modern 3D printing standard

### Features

- Interactive orbit controls

- Zoom & pan

- Auto-rotate option

- Configurable lighting

- Custom background color

- No external service — fully offline

### Technical Details

| Storage | Forge Storage (chunked base64 for large files) |
| --- | --- |
| External Service | None — Three.js renders client-side |
| Max File Size | ~4.5MB (Forge Storage limit) |
| Editor | Fullscreen config with 3D preview |
| Renderer | Three.js (WebGL) |
| Availability | Pro only |

### Limitations

- File size limited to ~4.5MB due to Forge Storage constraints (6MB Lambda payload minus base64 overhead)

- Very complex models with high polygon counts may impact page performance

- Textures must be embedded in GLB format — external texture references not supported

## Privacy Policy

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/privacy.html

[← Back to Home](https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/index.html)

## Privacy Policy

Last updated: June 2026 · Effective: June 1, 2026

### 1. Introduction

This Privacy Policy describes how Vectored ("we", "us", "our") handles information in connection with the Confluence Macro Toolkit application ("the App") distributed through the Atlassian Marketplace. We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of our users.

This policy applies to both the Lite (free) and Pro editions of the App.

### 2. Data We Do NOT Collect

The App does **not** collect, process, store, or transmit any of the following:

- Personal Identifiable Information (PII) — names, emails, addresses

- Usage analytics, telemetry, or behavioral data

- IP addresses, device fingerprints, or browser information

- Cookies, tracking pixels, or advertising identifiers

- Content of diagrams, markdown, polls, or any user-created macro content

**One thing to be clear about: this documentation website is not the App.** The site you are reading right now (docs.vectored.dev) uses cookieless analytics to count page views, described in the [main privacy policy](https://docs.vectored.dev/privacy.html#website). That measures *documentation pages* only. It collects nothing from Macro Toolkit inside Confluence, sees none of your macro content, and does not change anything above — installing and using the App still sends us nothing.

### 3. Data Storage & Processing

All data created by the App remains entirely within your Atlassian Confluence instance:

| Macro content | Stored as Confluence macro config parameters (inline with page content) — never leaves your instance |
| --- | --- |
| Poll votes | Stored in Forge Storage (Atlassian-managed, encrypted at rest) — scoped to your site only |
| Mood entries | Stored in Forge Storage — scoped to your site only |
| Admin settings | Stored in Forge Storage — accessible only by site admins |
| Draw.io diagrams | Stored in Forge Storage + page attachments — within your instance |

Forge Storage is Atlassian's managed storage service. Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2+. Storage is isolated per-app and per-site. We have no access to your stored data.

### 4. External Services

Most macros operate entirely client-side with no external calls. Two optional macros (disabled by default) connect to external services:

| Service | Used By | Data Sent | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| embed.diagrams.net | Draw.io macro | Diagram XML | Editor rendering |
| www.plantuml.com | PlantUML macro | PlantUML text (during editing only) | SVG rendering |

- Both are disabled by default — admin must explicitly enable them

- PlantUML: only sends text during editing; published page renders stored SVG offline

- No personal data or authentication tokens are sent to either service

- No other third-party analytics, advertising, or data-processing services are used

### 5. Atlassian API Scopes

The App requests the following Atlassian scopes, used solely for macro functionality:

| read:confluence-content.summary | Read page metadata to render macros in context |
| --- | --- |
| read:confluence-user | Resolve display names for poll/mood voter attribution |
| write:confluence-file | Upload diagram attachments (Draw.io only) |
| storage:app | Persist poll votes, mood data, admin settings, Draw.io diagrams |

These scopes follow the principle of least privilege. The App does not request write access to page content, user management, or space administration.

### 6. Data Retention & Deletion

- **Uninstall:** Running `forge uninstall` removes all Forge Storage data for that site

- **Macro content:** Deleting a page removes all inline macro config data

- **No backups:** We do not maintain any copies of your data outside Atlassian infrastructure

- **No data export:** We never export, aggregate, or access your instance data

### 7. Security Measures

- Runs on Atlassian Forge — sandboxed execution environment

- No server-side code outside Atlassian infrastructure

- All communication over TLS 1.2+

- Content Security Policy (CSP) enforced on all Custom UI resources

- Source code publicly auditable (open source)

### 8. Children's Privacy

The App is a business productivity tool and is not directed at children under 16. We do not knowingly collect data from children.

### 9. GDPR & International Compliance

Since the App does not collect or process personal data, GDPR data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability) are not applicable to our App directly. Your Confluence instance data is governed by your organization's agreement with Atlassian.

For GDPR purposes: we act as neither a data controller nor data processor, as no personal data flows through our systems.

### 10. Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated "Last updated" date. Material changes will be noted in the app's changelog. Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance.

### 11. Contact

If you have questions about this policy or our privacy practices:

- [Open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/openAPI-Studio/confluence-macro-toolkit/issues)

- Use the [Support page](https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/support.html) feedback form

- Email [support@vectored.dev](mailto:support@vectored.dev)

## Security Policy

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/security.html

[← Back to Home](https://docs.vectored.dev/macrotoolkit/index.html)

## Security Policy

Last updated: June 2026

### 1. Architecture & Execution Environment

Confluence Macro Toolkit runs entirely on the **Atlassian Forge platform** — a sandboxed, serverless execution environment managed by Atlassian.

**No custom backend servers.** All resolver logic executes in Forge's sandboxed Node.js runtime. We do not operate any servers, databases, or infrastructure.

**Sandboxed execution.** Forge enforces strict isolation between apps. Our code cannot access other apps' data, file systems, or network beyond declared permissions.

**Custom UI isolation.** All macro UIs run in sandboxed iframes with strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers enforced by Atlassian.

### 2. Network Security

| Encryption in transit | All communication uses TLS 1.2+ (enforced by Forge) |
| --- | --- |
| Encryption at rest | Forge Storage uses AES-256 encryption |
| Outbound connections | Only `embed.diagrams.net` and `plantuml.com` — both disabled by default |
| Inbound connections | None — no webhooks, no public endpoints |
| DNS/egress filtering | Forge restricts egress to declared domains in manifest.yml only |

### 3. Content Security Policy (CSP)

All Custom UI resources are served with Atlassian's strict CSP headers:

- `script-src 'self'` — no inline scripts except those bundled

- `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — required for Swagger UI rendering

- `connect-src` — restricted to Forge bridge API only

- `frame-src` — only `embed.diagrams.net` (when enabled)

### 4. Authentication & Authorization

- **No credentials stored.** The App never handles user passwords or tokens

- **Forge-managed auth.** All API calls use Forge's built-in token management

- **Admin-only settings.** Macro toggle settings require Confluence admin privileges

- **Scoped permissions.** Follows least-privilege — no write access to page content or user management

### 5. Input Validation & XSS Prevention

- All user input (diagram code, poll options, markdown) is sanitized before rendering

- Markdown rendered with DOMPurify sanitization to prevent XSS

- Mermaid diagrams rendered via official library with SVG output (no innerHTML)

- Poll/mood inputs length-limited and character-restricted

- Forge bridge communication validates message origin

### 6. Supply Chain Security

- **Open source.** Full source code publicly auditable on GitHub

- **Pinned dependencies.** All npm packages use exact versions (package-lock.json)

- **Minimal dependencies.** Each macro bundles only what it needs

- **No post-install scripts.** Build process is deterministic and auditable

### 7. Vulnerability Reporting

Responsible Disclosure

If you discover a security vulnerability, please **do not** open a public GitHub issue.

Instead:

1. Use GitHub's **private vulnerability reporting** feature on the repository

2. Or email [security@vectored.dev](mailto:security@vectored.dev)

We aim to acknowledge reports within 48 hours and provide a fix timeline within 7 days.

### 8. Incident Response

- Security patches released as priority updates

- Affected users notified via GitHub release notes and Marketplace changelog

- Post-incident analysis published for critical vulnerabilities

### 9. Compliance

| SOC 2 | Inherited from Atlassian Forge infrastructure |
| --- | --- |
| GDPR | No personal data processed — see Privacy Policy |
| CCPA | No personal information sold or shared |
| Forge Security Review | Subject to Atlassian's Marketplace security scanning |

## Forms & Frontdoor

by Vectored · for Confluence

Build custom forms in Confluence with a visual builder, 13 field types, theming, and access control — then let post-submit automation create Confluence pages, open Jira issues, and post to Slack or Teams. Responses stay in your Atlassian site.

### How to Use

1. Open the **Forms Dashboard** from Confluence global navigation

2. Click **New Form** — the canvas builder opens

3. Add questions using the type selector (text, email, date, signature, etc.)

4. Configure styling, access control, and collaboration in the settings drawers

5. Click **Preview** to test, then **Publish**

6. Embed on any page using the `/Forms & Frontdoor` macro

7. View responses in the Dashboard → Results tab, export as CSV

## Getting Started

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/getting-started.html

Get Forms & Frontdoor running on your Confluence site in under 2 minutes.

### 1. Installation

Install Forms & Frontdoor directly from the [Atlassian Marketplace](https://marketplace.atlassian.com). Search for **Forms & Frontdoor**, click **Install**, and authorize the app for your site. Once installed, it appears in your Confluence apps list and is ready to use immediately.

### 2. Opening the Dashboard

Navigate to **Apps > Forms & Frontdoor Dashboard** from your Confluence top navigation. The dashboard shows all forms on your site with search and filter controls so you can quickly find what you need.

### 3. Creating Your First Form

Click **New Form** to open the builder canvas. Add questions by clicking the **+ Add Question** button. Choose from field types like short text, multiple choice, date pickers, and more. Drag to reorder, and your form saves automatically.

![Forms & Frontdoor Builder](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/new form editor.png)

### 4. Embedding on a Page

Edit any Confluence page and type `/form` (or search for "Forms & Frontdoor") to insert the macro. Click the pencil icon on the macro to open configuration, then select the form you want to embed.

![Searching for Forms & Frontdoor macro](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/macro search.png) ![Selecting a form in macro config](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/form selector in macro editor.png)

## Building Forms

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/building-forms.html

The Forms & Frontdoor builder is a unified canvas editor where you design forms visually.

### The Builder Canvas

The canvas displays a centered form preview where you edit titles and descriptions inline. What you see is what respondents get — a true WYSIWYG experience.

![Builder canvas](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/new form editor.png)

### Adding Questions

Click **+ Add Question** to open the field picker. Choose from 13 field types — each represented by its own icon for quick identification.

### Question Configuration

Hover any question to reveal its toolbar: a **Required** toggle, a **Settings gear**, and a **Delete** button. Click the gear to access advanced settings including tooltip text, placeholder, and default value.

![Question settings](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/question with general and vaitation settings menu opened for single text.png)

### Rich Text Labels

Question labels support **Bold**, *Italic*, and [Link](#) formatting via a mini toolbar that appears when editing a label.

### Sections Pro

Add multiple sections with **+ Add Section** at the bottom of the canvas. Sections are edited in a stacked view — each with a numbered header, inline title, and its own Add Question control — while respondents see them as separate pages with Next and Back navigation. See [Multi-Section Forms](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/multi-section.html).

![Multi-section](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/section adition.png)

### Success Screen

Design what respondents see after submitting: title, message, and either a **success icon** (built-in drawn icons or any emoji from the picker) or a custom completion image. A live preview in the panel shows the result as you type.

### Post-Submit Automation

From the **Action** panel, open the Automation Builder to run Confluence, Jira, Slack, or Teams actions after each submission — with conditions, branching, and batching. See [Automation](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/automation.html).

#### Group Picker

Search and select Confluence groups. Single or multi-group mode. Requires authentication.

URL input with domain whitelist validation, HTTPS enforcement, and custom error messages.

## Smart Values

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/smart-values.html

Dynamic tokens that auto-fill based on who's viewing the form, where it's embedded, and when it's submitted.

### How to Use

In the form builder, click the `{x}` button next to any supported input (tooltip, placeholder, or default value). Select a token from the categorized dropdown to insert it.

Smart values can also be typed directly into form titles, descriptions, question labels, and taglines using the `{{token.name}}` syntax.

When a user opens the form, all tokens resolve to real values automatically. Tokens in the builder show as colored chips for easy identification.

### Where Smart Values Work

#### Form Title

e.g. "Feedback from {{user.name}}"

#### Form Description

e.g. "Submitted via {{space.name}}"

#### Question Labels

e.g. "Hi {{user.name}}, rate us"

#### Tagline / Description

e.g. "Your timezone: {{user.timezone}}"

#### Placeholder Text

e.g. "{{user.email}}"

#### Default Value

Pre-fills the field with resolved value

#### Info Tooltip

e.g. "Logged in as {{user.name}}"

### Available Tokens

#### User

| Token | Description | Example Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{user.name}} | Display name of logged-in user | Akshay KG |
| {{user.email}} | Email address | akshay@example.com |
| {{user.id}} | Atlassian account ID | 5daff052... |
| {{user.timezone}} | Browser timezone | Asia/Kolkata |
| {{user.language}} | Browser language preference | en-IN |
| {{user.localtime}} | User's current local time | 11:46:32 PM |

#### Page & Space

| Token | Description | Example Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{space.key}} | Key of the space containing the page | DEV |
| {{space.name}} | Name of the Confluence space | Development |
| {{page.title}} | Title of the page where form is embedded | Team Onboarding |
| {{site.url}} | Confluence site base URL | https://acme.atlassian.net |

#### Form

| Token | Description | Example Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{form.title}} | Title of the current form | Employee Feedback |
| {{form.id}} | Unique form identifier | 29f46b91-c3ca... |

#### Submission

| Token | Description | Example Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{submit.date}} | Current date when form loads | 20/06/2026 |
| {{submit.time}} | Current time when form loads | 11:46:32 PM |
| {{submit.datetime}} | ISO date-time string | 2026-06-20T23:46:32Z |

### Notes

- **Anonymous users:** User tokens resolve to "Anonymous" or empty when the respondent is not logged in.

- **Page/Space tokens:** Only available when the form is embedded via the macro on a Confluence page. Direct links won't have space/page context.

- **Stored values:** Tokens are stored as-is in the form schema. They resolve at display time, so each respondent sees their own personalized values.

- **Color coding:** In the builder, tokens display as colored inline chips — purple for user, teal for space/page, amber for form, green for submission.

## Validation & Constraints

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/validation.html

Forms & Frontdoor lets you enforce data quality with built-in validation rules on every field type.

### Required Fields

Toggle any question as required to prevent submission without an answer. A red asterisk appears next to required fields.

### Min/Max Length (Text)

Set minimum and maximum character limits on text fields. Respondents see a live character count and cannot submit if limits are violated.

### Min/Max Value (Numbers)

For number fields, define acceptable numeric ranges. Values outside the range trigger an inline error message.

### Regex Patterns

Apply custom regular expression patterns for advanced validation — useful for emails, phone numbers, or any structured input format.

### Custom Error Messages

Override default error text with your own messages to guide respondents clearly when validation fails.

### Per-Section Validation

In multi-section forms, validation runs when the user clicks Next — they cannot advance until all fields in the current section pass.

![Validation settings panel for a single text question](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/question with general and vaitation settings menu opened for single text.png)

## Multi-Section Forms Pro

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/multi-section.html

Break long forms into multiple pages with built-in navigation. This feature is available on the Pro tier.

### Adding Sections — Stacked View

Sections are edited in a single **stacked view**: they appear one after another inside the form canvas, so you always see the whole form. Click **+ Add Section** at the bottom of the canvas to append one.

- Each section has a header with its number, an inline title field, and a live question count.

- Every section gets its own **+ Add Question** control.

- Deleting a section that contains questions asks for confirmation first; empty sections delete instantly.

### Navigation

While the builder shows sections stacked, respondents see one section per page — they navigate with Next and Back buttons, and the Submit button only appears on the final section.

### Per-Section Validation

Validation is enforced per section — users must complete all required fields and pass constraints before advancing to the next section.

![Adding sections in the form builder](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/section adition.png)

1. Type `/form` in the page editor

Share forms outside of Confluence pages using direct links. Open the Share modal to access three tabs: Link (direct URL), Embed (iframe code), and ID (form identifier for API use).

## Styling & Theming

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/styling.html

Customize the look and feel of your forms with themes, colors, banners, and typography options.

### Theme Templates

Choose from 6 standard themes included with the free tier. Pro users get access to 7 additional live animated themes with dynamic backgrounds.

### Accent Color

Use the color picker to set an accent color that applies to buttons, progress bars, and highlights throughout your form.

### Banner Images

Pick a banner from the built-in preset gallery — there are separate sets for **light mode** and **dark mode** viewers. Each respondent automatically sees the variant matching their own Confluence theme.

- Choosing a preset auto-selects its matching counterpart in the other mode, so both are always covered.

- Pick **None** to fall back to a gradient banner in your accent color, with an optional decoration pattern.

### Success Screen Icon

In the **Success Screen** panel, choose the icon shown after submission: one of the built-in drawn icons (checkmark, trophy, star, heart, rocket, and more) or any emoji from the picker. A custom completion image, when set, takes precedence over the icon.

### Banner Decorations

Add decorative overlays to your banner: circles, diamonds, waves, dots, or none.

### Typography & Layout

Select from available fonts, adjust form width (standard, wide, or full), and choose a question numbering style to match your brand.

![Theme and styling settings panel](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/theme setting.png)

## Access Control

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/access-control.html

Control who can view and submit your forms with flexible access levels.

### Access Levels

Choose who can access your form:

- **Anonymous** — anyone with the link can submit (no login required)

- **Logged-in users** — only authenticated Confluence users

- **Specific groups** — restrict to selected Confluence groups

### Single Submission Limit

Enable the single-submission toggle to allow each user only one response. Subsequent attempts show a lock screen indicating the form has already been completed.

### Lock Screens

Unauthorized users or those who have exceeded submission limits see a lock screen explaining why they cannot access the form.

![Access control and submission limit settings](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/access and limit settings.png)

## Collaboration

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/collaboration.html

Share form ownership and editing access with your team members.

### Co-Owners & Editors

Add collaborators by searching for users in your Confluence instance. Grant them co-owner or editor access to work on forms together.

### Shared Access

Collaborators can edit form structure, view and export responses, and manage settings based on their permission level.

### Permission-Based Access

Editors can modify form fields and content. Co-owners have full control including access settings, deletion, and managing other collaborators.

![Co-owner and editor collaboration settings](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/co owner and editor settings.png)

## Responses & Export

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/responses.html

View, manage, and export all form submissions from a centralized response table.

### Response Table

All submissions are displayed in a table with one column per form field. Signature fields show as thumbnails inline.

### CSV Export

Click the CSV export button to download all responses as a spreadsheet-compatible file for offline analysis.

### Save as PDF

Optionally enable a "Save as PDF" button on the thank-you screen so respondents can download a copy of their submission. Toggle this in the Action settings panel.

![Response table with CSV export button highlighted](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/response view with csv export heighlited.png)

## Automation

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/automation.html

Run actions automatically after every form submission — create Confluence pages, open Jira issues, post to Slack or Teams, branch with If / Else conditions, and process responses one-by-one or in batches. Open it from the builder: **Action → Automation → Open Automation Builder**.

### The Automation Canvas

Automations are built on a visual canvas: a trigger chip (*On form submit*) at the top, a vertical flow of step cards, and an *End* marker. Insert steps anywhere with the **+** buttons on the connector line.

- Each step card shows a provider color strip, a summary of its configuration, an on/off toggle, and a **⋯** menu (Configure / Duplicate / Delete).

- Duplicating a condition clones its entire Then / Else subtree.

- The master pill in the command bar turns the whole automation on or off without deleting anything.

![Automation canvas with a trigger, action steps, and an If/Else branch](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/automation canvas with simple automation built.png)

### Actions

All configuration fields marked with the smart-value inserter accept tokens like `{{form.title}}`, `{{answer.field_name}}`, or `{{response.table}}`.

**Confluence** — Create page, Add comment, Append to page, Create task (with assignee), Add label, Add watcher, Add attachment (saves response data as a file on a page).

**Jira** — Create issue (project, type, priority, assignee, labels), Comment on issue, Set priority, Add watcher. Jira actions require Jira on the same site with the app installed; otherwise they show a *Needs Jira* badge.

**Slack** — Send a message to a channel via an incoming webhook URL (hooks.slack.com). Create one in Slack under channel → Integrations → Incoming Webhooks.

**Microsoft Teams** — Send a message via a Teams *Workflows* webhook. In Teams: channel → Workflows → "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received", then paste the generated URL.

**Webhook (generic)** — marked Coming Soon.

![Add-step panel with searchable action catalog](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/automation step pallet.png)

### If / Else Branching

Add an **If / Else branch** to split the flow. Conditions use the same rule engine as dashboard filters — pick a field, an operator, and a value, or match free text.

- Submissions matching the rules follow the **Then** lane; everything else follows **Else**.

- Each lane holds its own list of actions with individual toggles.

- A branch with no condition set runs Then for every submission (the card warns you).

- After the lanes, the flow rejoins and continues with all submissions.

### Run Modes: After Each vs. In Batches

**After each** — the flow runs once per submission, immediately.

**In batches** — submissions queue up until the batch size is reached (default 25, configurable 2–500), then the flow runs once for the whole batch. Leftover submissions flush automatically every hour, so partial batches are never stuck.

- In batch mode, `{{response.table}}` and `{{response.json}}` aggregate the whole batch, and `{{batch.count}}` gives its size.

- If / Else splits the batch: Then runs once with the matching submissions, Else once with the rest. Empty groups are skipped and logged.

### Run As & Permissions

Choose whether actions run as the **App** (recommended) or as the **Submitter**. Run-as-submitter is unavailable while the form allows anonymous responses.

Saving an automation runs a **permission preflight**: every enabled action is checked against what *you* (the author) can personally do — e.g. edit permission on a target page, or create permission in a Jira project. Failing steps are highlighted with the reason. The same check re-runs at execution time, so an author who later loses access can't keep automating past it.

### Test Runs & Logs

**Test run** performs a dry run against your latest submission (no real actions executed) and shows the path taken through conditions plus each action's resolved configuration.

The **Automation** tab in a form's results view shows the execution log: every action run with status (success / error / skipped), message, and timestamp. Batch runs are grouped by batch ID.

![Automation execution log with per-action statuses](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/automation result log screenshot.png)

### Site-Wide Master Switch

Confluence admins can disable automation site-wide from **Forms & Frontdoor Settings**. While off, flows can still be drafted and saved but won't run — the builder shows a warning banner.

## Dashboard

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/docs/dashboard.html

Manage all your forms from the Forms & Frontdoor dashboard — search, sort, and take actions at a glance.

### Search & Sort

Use the search bar to find forms by name. Sort by newest, oldest, alphabetical, or **most responses**. The header summarises your library — e.g. "5 forms · 3 owned · 2 shared with you".

### Form Cards

Forms are displayed in a card grid. Each card shows at a glance:

- An accent color strip matching the form's theme

- An **Owner** or **Editor** badge — your role on that form

- The form description

- Stats: response count, field count, and how many people have edit access

- Created date and time of the last response

### Quick Actions

Each form card provides quick actions:

- **Edit** — open the form builder

- **Share** — direct link, embed instructions, and form ID

- **Duplicate** — clone the form (you become the copy's owner)

- **Results** — responses table, analytics dashboard, and automation logs

- **Delete** — owner only; removes the form and all responses after confirmation

Forms & Frontdoor by Vectored

![Forms & Frontdoor dashboard with form cards](https://docs.vectored.dev/forms/assets/response view with csv export heighlited.png)

AWS SES notifications with editable templates and smart values.

](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/email-notifications.html) [

#### Company Values

Tag recognitions with the values your company celebrates.

](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/company-values.html) [

#### Moderation

Flagging, review queue, and admin controls.

](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/moderation.html)

GIF search in the composer is![Powered by GIPHY](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/giphy-attribution-dark.svg)with an admin-set workplace content-rating ceiling.

### How It Works

1. Open **Recognition Hub** from Confluence or Jira global navigation

2. Click **+ Give recognition** and pick a card template

3. Or describe the occasion and let **AI** draft the title, message, value and GIF for you

4. Search teammates, write your kudos, tag a company value, add a GIF

5. Post — the card lands on the live mural and recipients get a rich email

6. The team reacts with emoji and comments; share cards by link, email, or page macro

## Getting Started

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/getting-started.html

Install Recognition Hub and post your first recognition

### 1. Installation

Recognition Hub is available on the **Atlassian Marketplace** for Confluence and Jira Cloud. Install it from the Marketplace listing, authorize the app for your site, and it appears under **Apps** in your Confluence or Jira navigation. Free for teams of up to 10 users.

### 2. Opening the Hub

Navigate to **Apps > Recognition Hub** from the Confluence or Jira top navigation. The hub is a live mural of recognition cards — it auto-refreshes every 30 seconds, loads more as you scroll, and follows your Confluence light/dark theme automatically.

![The Recognition Hub recognition mural](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/recognition dashboard.png)

### 3. Posting Your First Recognition

Click **+ Give recognition** in the header. Pick a card template, search for the teammates you want to recognize, write a short title and message, optionally tag a company value and attach a GIF, then post. The card appears at the top of the mural instantly and recipients are notified by email.

**Email leaves the Atlassian platform.** To reach a recipient’s inbox, notification email is sent through AWS SES, so that content transits AWS — not just Atlassian. For complete data locality, configure your **own AWS SES credentials** under **Settings > Email** so mail routes through infrastructure you control. See [Email Notifications](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/email-notifications.html).

![Posting a recognition](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/posting recognition page.png)

### 4. Admin Setup

Site admins configure Recognition Hub under **Settings > Recognition Hub** (Confluence or Jira): connect a GIPHY key (or use the built-in one), define company values, set up email notifications, and manage moderation.

![GIPHY connection settings](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/GIPHY configuration settingfspage.png)

[Get Recognition Hub on the Atlassian Marketplace →](https://marketplace.atlassian.com/apps/564712405)

## Giving Recognition

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/giving-recognition.html

Card templates, recipients, company values, and GIFs

### Card Templates

Every recognition starts from a template that shapes how the card renders on the mural: **Classic** (accent bar), **Spotlight** (GIF-forward, double width), **Milestone** (celebratory), **Minimal Quote** (short shout-outs), and **Team Shout** (group recognitions, double width).

![The recognition composer with templates, recipients, values and GIFs](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/posting recognition page.png)

### Recipients

Search any teammate by name (Confluence or Jira) and add up to 20 recipients per recognition. Self-recognition is blocked — recognition is for celebrating *others*. For multi-recipient posts, everyone is included on one notification email.

**Email leaves the Atlassian platform.** To reach a recipient’s inbox, notification email is sent through AWS SES, so that content transits AWS — not just Atlassian. For complete data locality, configure your **own AWS SES credentials** under **Settings > Email** so mail routes through infrastructure you control. See [Email Notifications](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/email-notifications.html).

### Company Values

Optionally tag the recognition with one of your company's values. The value renders as a colored chip on the card and in the notification email, and can be curated by admins (up to 10 values).

### GIFs

GIF search is powered by GIPHY ![Powered by GIPHY](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/giphy-attribution-dark.svg) — the composer offers a searchable picker with trending GIFs and full search. GIFs render full-size on cards and appear as a still frame in notification emails.

#### How the GIPHY integration works

- **Built-in or workspace key** — GIFs work out of the box with the app’s built-in GIPHY key; admins can override it with their own workspace key under **Settings > Connections** (write-only, stored encrypted, with a test-connection button).

- **Content-rating ceiling** — admins cap results at G, PG, or PG-13 (the workplace maximum). Every GIPHY request is filtered to that rating or stricter.

- **Hotlinked, never re-hosted** — GIF media is served straight from GIPHY’s CDN per GIPHY’s terms of service. Nothing is copied or stored by the app; only the GIF URL and attribution metadata are saved.

- **Attribution everywhere** — the mandatory “Powered by GIPHY” mark is shown in the picker, on card media, and in emails. Admins can disable GIFs entirely at any time.

![GIPHY connection settings with content rating and test connection](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/GIPHY configuration settingfspage.png)

## AI Assist

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/ai-assist.html

Draft recognitions and polish messages with Atlassian-hosted AI

Runs on Atlassian No API key. No data leaves the Atlassian platform.

AI Assist is powered by **Forge LLMs** — Atlassian-hosted Claude models that run entirely inside the Atlassian platform. There is no third-party AI key to configure and nothing to send to an external service. It adds two things to the composer: a **Draft with AI** starting point and a one-click **Quick rewrite** for the message.

### Draft with AI

When AI Assist is on, **Give recognition** opens with a Draft with AI panel above the card templates (the button also picks up a ✨ sparkle). Describe what someone did in plain language and Recognition Hub drafts the whole card for you:

- **Title** — a short, punchy headline.

- **Message** — a warm note written in the second person.

- **Company value** — the best-matching value from your workspace, auto-selected (or none).

- **GIF** — a mood-appropriate GIPHY search runs automatically and the top result is pre-selected.

The draft lands on the compose step with everything filled in and the cursor parked on the **recipient** field — you just add the people and post. Nothing is submitted automatically, and every field stays fully editable. Press ⌘/Ctrl + Enter in the description box to draft without reaching for the mouse.

![The Give recognition dialog with the Draft with AI panel above the card templates](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/New give recognition popup with draft with ai showing.png)

### Quick rewrite

Already wrote a message but want it tighter or warmer? Click **✨ Quick rewrite** next to the Message field. AI Assist returns a polished version — keeping your meaning and any names — as a suggestion you can preview, then **Use this** to drop it into the card or **Dismiss** to keep your original.

![The Quick rewrite suggestion shown beneath the message field with Use this and Dismiss actions](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/AI description rewrite screen shot.png)

### Admin controls

AI Assist has its own tab under **Settings > AI Assist**. It is on by default; admins can turn it off site-wide at any time, which immediately hides Draft with AI and Quick rewrite for everyone.

- **Enable AI assist in the composer** — the single on/off switch for the whole site.

- **Test AI** — a live check that confirms the site can reach Forge LLMs and reports whether AI is currently available.

- **Graceful fallback** — if a site can't use Atlassian AI (for example, it's blocked by policy or not provisioned), the AI controls quietly disappear and the composer works exactly as before.

![The AI Assist admin tab with the enable toggle, Test AI button, and availability status](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/AI assistant settings.png)

### Privacy & billing

- **Runs on Atlassian** — requests are processed by Atlassian-hosted models under Atlassian's security and compliance; no external AI provider is involved and no API key is needed.

- **Same moderation as first-party AI** — prompts pass the same safety checks as Atlassian's own AI features.

- **Only what you type** — the model sees the occasion or message you provide plus your workspace's company-value names, nothing more.

- **Included, usage-based** — AI usage is billed to the app, not to your site. There's no separate AI subscription to buy.

## Reactions & Comments

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/reactions-comments.html

Celebrate posts with emoji reactions, confetti, and comments

### Reactions

Every card shows three quick reactions (🎉 👏 ❤️) plus a **+** button that opens a 16-emoji palette. Reactions are persisted, counted across the team, and toggling one fires a confetti burst contained inside the card. Counts update live for everyone via the feed's 30-second refresh.

### Comments

Add short congratulation comments under any card. Comments are persisted, show the author's name and avatar, and are included in the live refresh so conversations stay current without reloading.

### Live Updates

The mural polls every 30 seconds (pausing while the tab is hidden) and offers a manual refresh button next to the “Updated just now” indicator. New cards slide in with an entrance animation; existing cards update reaction and comment counts in place.

## Sharing & Page Macro

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/sharing-and-macro.html

Direct links, email sharing, and embedding cards on pages

### Share Dialog

Every card has a share button (share icon) opening three tabs: **Direct link**, **Email**, and **Macro ID**.

![The share dialog with Direct link, Email, and Macro ID tabs](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/share recognition popup.png)

### Direct Links

The direct link deep-links into the hub and opens that recognition as a popup over the mural — same link used in notification emails' “View this recognition” button. Anyone with access to your Atlassian site can open it.

### Sharing by Email

The Email tab lets you send the recognition to teammates on your site (searchable picker) *and* to raw email addresses for people the picker can't find. Sends use your configured email provider and the same rich template as notifications.

**Email leaves the Atlassian platform.** Everything else in Recognition Hub stays inside Atlassian, but to actually reach a recipient’s inbox, email must be delivered through AWS SES — so the message content (title, note, value, GIF still, deep link) transits AWS to be sent. With the built-in credentials, that path is the app’s AWS SES. **If you want complete data locality — no recognition data leaving infrastructure you control — set up your own AWS SES** (access key, region, verified from-address) under **Settings > Email**, so mail is sent through your own AWS account. Email is the only feature that egresses beyond Atlassian.

### Recognition Card Macro

The page macro is **Confluence only** — Jira has no page-macro equivalent. Copy the **Macro ID** from the share dialog, then on any Confluence page type `/Recognition Card`, insert the macro, and paste the ID. The live card — reactions and comments included — renders right on the page.

## Company Values

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/company-values.html

Tag recognitions with the values your company celebrates

### What They Are

Company values are the tags your team celebrates — *Ownership*, *Customer Obsession*, *Craftsmanship*, and whatever else defines your culture. A tagged recognition shows the value as a colored chip on the card and in the email.

### Managing Values

Admins manage values under **Settings > Company Values**: add (up to 10), rename inline, toggle active, or delete. Colors are assigned automatically from a curated palette so the set always looks coherent — no color picking required.

![Company Values admin settings](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/company value settings page.png)

### Defaults

New installations start with five sensible defaults you can keep, rename, or replace entirely.

## Email Notifications

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/email-notifications.html

AWS SES notifications with editable templates and smart values

### How Notifications Work

When a recognition is posted, one email goes out per recognition: all recognized users in **To**, the sender in **Cc**. The email is a rich, branded card — title, message, value chip, GIF still frame, and a deep link back to the recognition. Self-recognitions never send mail.

### AWS SES

Delivery uses **AWS SES**. The app ships with built-in credentials so email works out of the box, and admins can override with their own AWS access key, region, and SES-verified from-address under **Settings > Email** (credentials are write-only and stored encrypted). A test-send button verifies the setup.

**Email leaves the Atlassian platform.** Everything else in Recognition Hub stays inside Atlassian, but to actually reach a recipient’s inbox, email must be delivered through AWS SES — so the message content (title, note, value, GIF still, deep link) transits AWS to be sent. With the built-in credentials, that path is the app’s AWS SES. **If you want complete data locality — no recognition data leaving infrastructure you control — set up your own AWS SES** (access key, region, verified from-address) under **Settings > Email**, so mail is sent through your own AWS account. Email is the only feature that egresses beyond Atlassian.

![AWS SES email settings with test send](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/ses configuration settings page.png)

### Editable Templates

Under **Settings > Email Templates**, each template opens in a full-screen editor (subject, HTML body, plain-text body) with a click-to-copy **smart values** panel — placeholders like `{{senderName}}`, `{{recipientNames}}`, `{{currentDate}}` that resolve at send time. Conditional sections show content only when a value exists. One click restores the shipped defaults.

## Moderation

Source: https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/docs/moderation.html

Flagging, review queue, and admin controls

### Flagging

Every card has a flag button (flag icon). Any user can flag a recognition as potentially offensive, picking a reason (offensive/inappropriate, spam, other). A flagged recognition is **hidden from everyone immediately** — the mural, deep links, and page macros all treat it as under review.

![The flag and hide dialog with reason options](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/flag and hide popup.png)

### Review Queue

Admins resolve flags under **Settings > Moderation**. The queue shows each flagged card with its author, recipients, date, who flagged it, and the reason. **Unflag** restores it everywhere; **Delete** removes it permanently along with its reactions and comments.

![The moderation review queue](https://docs.vectored.dev/rewardhub/assets/Moderation settings pahe.png)

### Finding Any Recognition

The same screen searches *all* recognitions by title or message (not just flagged ones), so admins can locate and remove any post on request.

# Lens

## Lens

## Lens

by Vectored · for Chrome

COMING SOON

Capture a region of any tab as a PNG, an animated GIF or an MP4, or click through a flow and get a step-by-step guide out of it — annotated, named, and filed straight into a folder on your own machine with a metadata timeline beside it. No account, no upload, no server.

[Read the Docs](https://docs.vectored.dev/lens/docs/getting-started.html) [Ask for early access](https://docs.vectored.dev/lens/support.html)

![Lens capturing a region of a web page, with the selection toolbar and the extension popup visible](https://docs.vectored.dev/lens/assets/lens-hero.png)
